_comment: KNOWN-GAP REPRODUCTION for the WRONG way to declare this block's well
tie. Not an item-11 artifact -- never cite this run as evidence about
this block.
Byte-identical to the supply spec except that the tie below drops the
`tap_requires` narrowing and declares a BARE `tap_layer` naming COMP
EXPECTED OUTCOME: `klt erc` classifies the tie as DEGENERATE
(klayout-tools#2199) and records its `erc.missing_tie` work in
`erc_coverage.skipped` with reason `degenerate_tap_declaration`,
downgrading `erc_status` from `clean` to `clean_partial`. It does NOT
report a clean well-tie verdict, and it does not report findings.
WHY IT STILL MATTERS AFTER ISSUE #356. A bare COMP tap layer matches
every source/drain contact inside the well, not just the drawn taps --
so on THIS stream, where every well genuinely is tapped, it would now
report a clean verdict for the wrong reason, and would go on reporting
one if the taps were deleted again. The refusal is what makes the
supply spec's `tap_requires: ["32/0"]` narrowing load-bearing rather
than decorative: the narrowing is the only form of this declaration
that can tell a tap from a source/drain contact.
This case is committed so the supply spec's narrowing is a MEASURED
choice with a re-runnable artifact behind it, not an assertion.
`run_erc.py` re-runs it and asserts the outcome above.
